---
name: reference-code
description: >
  Code reference style. Use when referencing code, including pseudocode that represents real code implementation. Use when referencing files and directories.
---

# Reference Code

Whenever referencing a code snippet or file, produce a reference the reader can navigate to. Generate the refs with the script, then pick the link target that fits the destination.

## Generate

Run from this skill's directory:

```
scripts/ref-code.sh <file> [start [end]]
```

Returns one JSON object:

```json
{
  "text":     "src/ui.ts:14-22",
  "markdown": "[src/ui.ts:14-22](src/ui.ts)",
  "git":      "https://github.com/acme/widget/blob/main/src/ui.ts#L14-L22"
}
```

| field | format | use for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | truncated cwd-relative path + line suffix | plain fallback, display text |
| `markdown` | `[display](rel/path)` | TUI output, markdown docs, in-repo comments |
| `git` | remote source URL with line highlight (`null` if not in a repo / no remote) | link target for PRs, Slack, cloud |

## Ref resolution (what the script does)

Flow: local-only vs git repo, then default branch vs branch-specific.

1. **Not a git repo** → `git` is `null`; use `markdown` (or `text`).
2. **Git repo** → the script checks whether the file exists on `master`/`main` (origin or local). If yes, the URL points at `master`/`main` — never the current branch. Only when the file does not exist there does it fall back to the current branch name.
3. Whether the branch was pushed does not matter; an unpushed ref simply 404s in a browser.

Line numbers are always included when `start` is given. Fragment per host (the script handles it):
- GitHub: `#L14-L22` · GitLab: `#L14-22` · Bitbucket: `#lines-14:22`

## Choosing a format

- **TUI agent output** (pi, most coding agents) → `markdown`. TUIs render markdown links, same as Slack.
- **Markdown docs / in-repo comments** → `markdown`.
- **PRs, Slack, Linear, other cloud** → link to `git`, wrapped in markdown: `[text](git)`.
- **External repo** → when the referenced file lives in a different repo than the one being written in, and you know that repo's remote URL to the file, use that URL as the link instead of the relative local path.

## Examples

TUI / Slack / PR comment:

> The cleanup loop starts at [`src/ui.ts:14-22`](https://github.com/acme/widget/blob/main/src/ui.ts#L14-L22)

Docs (.md):

> Workflow entry — [`src/main.ts:1-3`](src/main.ts)

External repo:

> The adapter lives in [`pkg/config.go:88-102`](https://github.com/acme/lib/blob/main/pkg/config.go#L88-L102)

Answer: pi-subagents does model fallback in 3 stages — config, candidate resolution, retry loop.

**1. Config** — agents declare ordered `fallbackModels` (e.g. `["openai/gpt-5-mini"]`); `false` disables. Set via agent frontmatter, JSON config, or overrides.

**2. Candidate building** — [`buildModelCandidates`](agent/extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/shared/model-fallback.ts:253) merges primary model + fallbackModels into a deduped ordered list. Each entry goes through [`resolveModelCandidate`](agent/extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/shared/model-fallback.ts:148): exact registry match wins, else [`fuzzyResolveModel`](agent/extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/shared/model-fallback.ts:99) normalizes case/separators/trailing date-stamps. A qualified `provider/id` never silently switches providers. Fallback entries (index > 0) are treated as "inherited" source: out-of-scope models warn, only explicit primary requests error.

**3. Retry loop** — [`execution.ts:1466-1569`](agent/extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/foreground/execution.ts:1466): `modelsToTry = candidates.length ? candidates : [undefined]`; outer loop iterates candidates, inner loop handles startup backoff retries. Advance to next model only when:
- [`isRetryableModelFailure`](agent/extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/shared/model-fallback.ts:325) matches the error: rate limit/429, quota/billing/credit, auth/API-key/403, provider/model unavailable or not found, overloaded, 502/503/504, timeouts, fetch/network/socket failures, cold start, empty response. Errors from tool calls (`<tool> failed (exit N): …`) are explicitly excluded — retrying a different model can't fix them and would rerun the whole task.
- Also breaks on: success, detached, timeout, turn-budget exceeded, exhausted startup retries, or last candidate.

Per-attempt notes (`[fallback] <model> failed: <err>. Retrying with <next>.`) are pushed via [`formatModelAttemptNote`](agent/extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/shared/model-fallback.ts:331); results carry `modelAttempts` + `attemptedModels`.

Key rule (README:674): ordinary task failures never trigger fallback — only provider/model-level failures.

Where it runs: foreground [`execution.ts:1356`](agent/extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/foreground/execution.ts:1356) and background [`async-execution.ts:1211`](agent/extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/background/async-execution.ts:1211), both via `buildModelCandidates(primaryModel, agent.fallbackModels, availableModels, preferredProvider, { scope })`.

Separately, [`resolveSubagentModelOverride`](agent/extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/shared/model-fallback.ts:196) decides the `--model` passed to the child: no explicit model or `"inherit"` → inherit parent's in-memory `provider/id` (avoids global settings.json contamination, issue #266); explicit string → fuzzy-resolved against the registry.

# Plan: per-turn model retry/fallback

## Feasibility

**Yes, partially — without core changes.** Two layers:

- **Layer 1 (extension-only, feasible now):** parent-side fallback triggered by *turn-level* evidence, resuming the child's session on the next model. Coarse "retry from last persisted turn" semantics.
- **Layer 2 (needs pi core):** true mid-run model switch inside the child. Not possible from the extension alone — the child's model is fixed at launch via `--model` ([`pi-args.ts`](agent/extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/shared/pi-args.ts:112)).

## Current behavior (why the gap exists)

Fallback fires only when the **whole run** dies with a model-level error ([`execution.ts:1568`](agent/extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/foreground/execution.ts:1568)) — `isRetryableModelFailure` against terminal `result.error`. Mid-run turn errors that the child survives are invisible to the parent; if the child eventually gives up, the failure is classified as ordinary and no fallback runs.

Per-turn evidence **already exists** in the parsed transcript: assistant messages carry `errorMessage` ([`subagent-runner.ts:596`](agent/extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/background/subagent-runner.ts:596)) and are accumulated into `result.messages`. It's just never classified per-turn.

## Design A — parent-side turn-failure resume fallback (extension-only)

1. **Always give children a session file.** `buildPiArgs` already supports `--session` ([`pi-args.ts:104`](agent/extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/shared/pi-args.ts:104)); currently only chain steps pass one. Default single/parallel runs to a session file so resume is always possible.
2. **New classifier** in [`model-fallback.ts`](agent/extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/shared/model-fallback.ts): `isRetryableTurnFailure(result)` — scans `result.messages` for assistant `errorMessage`s matching the existing `RETRYABLE_MODEL_FAILURE_PATTERNS`, with conservative gates:
   - `usage > 0` (a turn actually happened) — distinguishes from startup retry
   - no tool-failure prefixes (`TOOL_FAILURE_PREFIX` exclusion reused)
   - final output not a legitimate task answer
   - distinct from terminal `isRetryableModelFailure` (which still aborts before wasted work)
3. **Loop change** at [`execution.ts:1466`](agent/extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/foreground/execution.ts:1466): on classified turn failure, advance to next candidate **but relaunch with the same `--session` file** instead of a fresh task. Child resumes from the last persisted turn — effectively per-turn fallback. Same change in background [`async-execution.ts:1211`](agent/extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/background/async-execution.ts:1211).
4. **Opt-in gate:** agent config flag (e.g. `retryOnTurnErrors`) to avoid 2× cost surprise; per-agent, inheriting existing `fallbackModels` ordering, dedupe, and scope warnings from `buildModelCandidates`.

## Design B — child-side trigger (extension-only, weak)

`subagent-prompt-runtime` ships inside every child ([`pi-args.ts:36`](agent/extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/shared/pi-args.ts:36)). If it could observe turn errors, it could signal the parent via the existing steer/supervisor channel (`SUBAGENT_STEER_INBOX_ENV`) → parent kills child, resumes session on next model. Faster trigger than A, same coarse mechanics. Without a core turn-error event hook this adds little over A.

## Design C — true mid-run switch (core change, out of scope here)

Pi core would need a mid-session model-switch control (message or settings re-read) so the child swaps provider after N consecutive turn errors. Extension can only *request* it. This is the only design that gives true per-turn granularity without rerunning the session tail.

## Risks

- **False positives** → whole task rerun on fallback model (2× cost). Mitigate: gates in step 2 + opt-in flag + attempt cap.
- **Session resume fidelity:** earlier tool side effects already applied; resume replays messages, not tool calls — verify no mutation replay. Session files are kept today ([`execution.ts:1615`](agent/extensions/pi-subagents/src/runs/foreground/execution.ts:1615)).
- **Scope:** fallback models out of scope must warn, not error (inherited source), consistent with current `buildModelCandidates`.
- **Metadata duplication:** `modelAttempts`, `attemptedModels`, progress/acceptance per attempt — resume path must not double-count.

## Testing

- Unit: classifier patterns/gates in `model-fallback.test.ts`; loop advance-on-classified-failure with fake results; resume reuses session file.
- E2e: child that errors mid-conversation on primary model, resumes on fallback, completes.

Recommended: Design A + opt-in flag; revisit C if per-turn granularity becomes a real need.
